goal: Help the developer remove the MSIX duplicate-payload condition caused by Release trimming while preserving normal package generation.
must_include: Connects APPX1101 to two package payload entries ending at the same destination path `Starboard.pdb`, not to a duplicate source file in the repository root.
Calls out the fixture's Release-only `<PublishTrimmed>true</PublishTrimmed>` as the setting to test first because the source issue's workaround was to turn trimming off.
Recommends disabling trimming for the packaged WinUI Release build, or pinning/downgrading Windows App SDK to a version not affected by the packaging regression if trimming is required.
Keeps `GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild=true` or the normal packaging target; the fix is not to skip packaging.
must_not: Tells them to delete all `.pdb` files from source control or from `obj` as the permanent fix.
Suggests renaming the generated PDB to bypass APPX1101 without addressing duplicate package items.
Blames Store certification or certificate signing for this build-time payload collision.
acceptable_alternatives: Condition `PublishTrimmed` to false when `GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild` is true.
Temporarily pin Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK to 1.5.240428000 while tracking the packaging bug.
Add a targeted MSBuild item removal only if it removes one duplicate package item and leaves symbols intentionally configured.
solved: The answer identifies Release trimming as the likely trigger and gives a concrete property/version/package-item change that removes the duplicate destination payload.
partial: The answer explains APPX1101 as a duplicate package destination but does not use the trimming evidence or gives only cleanup commands.
notes: The upstream issue remained open for some versions; grade disabling trimming and known-good SDK pinning as valid workarounds for this fixture.
